The claim's predicted failure mode (a lone backslash left unmatched mid-token) does not occur, because the alternation is over single characters, not two-character units: '/' is already a member of the character class [A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-], and the separate \\\\ branch matches a lone literal backslash by itself. So a backslash is consumed by the \\\\ branch and the following slash is consumed by the character-class alternative (or trivially by the \\/ branch, which is merely a redundant escaped-slash form matching a single '/'); together they still consume both characters of the pair. The claim's characterization of ERE \\/ as 'an escaped / that matches a single literal slash only' is correct, but its conclusion that this leaves the backslash unmatched is false since the backslash has its own dedicated branch.","file_checked":"scripts/scrub-credentials.sh:64-65","property_proven":true,"inaccuracy_scope":"generated_claim_text"}
